notes: Ends at the start of the JSONL data-loss discussion. Observability and complete concurrency/test coverage are absent.

Identifies retry duplication and ordering risks, but presenting UPSERT/INSERT IGNORE/REPLACE as sufficient to ensure retries cannot corrupt data is too broad. Idempotency depends on keys and update semantics.

Official MySQL documentation describes REPLACE as deleting a conflicting old row before inserting; it cannot be assumed to preserve the intended update behavior. PostgreSQL permits arbitrary update expressions; repeated increments are a simple non-idempotent counterexample.
